proposals.impact: convert 2 stranded intro-load sessions into quiz starts
proposals.observation: Two sessions landed on the quiz intro screen in the last 48 hours. Neither one moved past intro_load. Start count is zero. These are not bounce-and-gone visitors — they loaded the page, which means they read something upstream that made them curious enough to click. The drop happens at the first moment of commitment: the point where they are asked to begin. The intro screen is carrying all the weight of the sell, and it is losing both visitors at that single step.
proposals.proposal: The quiz intro copy almost certainly leads with what the quiz IS (a money personality quiz, a quick assessment, etc.) rather than why picking up the phone on your own patterns matters right now, today. Rewrite the intro paragraph to open with a specific, grounded observation that names the tension the ICP already feels — the gap between earning decently and still not building anything — then move directly to a short, plain-English call to action. Remove any framing that sounds like a personality-test novelty. The goal is to make starting feel like the obvious next move, not a gamble on whether the output will be worth their time.
proposals.current_text: Take our free quiz to discover your money personality type and understand why you behave the way you do around money.
proposals.new_text:
You earn enough that money shouldn't feel this complicated. But something keeps getting in the way — the ignored statement, the vague dread before a big purchase, the month that somehow ends the same way the last one did.

This takes about four minutes. It will show you the specific pattern underneath that feeling, drawn from your actual answers rather than a generic description.

Joel MSc Behavioural Economics | Qualified Financial Planner built this from the same behavioural research he uses with clients. Nothing is sold at the end.

Start when you're ready.

proposals.impact: capitalise on 66.67% open rate by strengthening sequence hook
proposals.observation: The Money Vigilance automation is opening at 66.67% — twelve sends, eight opens. That is the strongest performer across all three active sequences, running about fourteen percentage points ahead of Money Avoidance and nearly thirty ahead of Money Worship. A sequence with that open rate is one where the subject line and sender trust are already doing their job. The constraint now is almost certainly what happens inside the email: whether the body copy is specific enough to pull a reader toward the next email, or whether it settles for being interesting without being directional.
proposals.proposal: Strengthen the closing paragraph of email-01 in the Money Vigilance sequence. High open rates on email one do not automatically carry through to email two — the reader needs a reason grounded in their specific situation to stay. The current closer is probably a soft, general sign-off. Replace it with a sentence or two that names what a Money Vigilance pattern actually costs the reader in practical terms — not emotionally, practically — and tells them plainly what email two will address. No cliffhanger device, no false urgency. Just an honest statement of what is coming and why it is worth reading.
proposals.current_text: In the next email, we'll go deeper into what your money vigilance pattern means for your financial future. Keep an eye out for it.
proposals.new_text: The next email gets specific about one practical consequence most people with this pattern don't spot until it's already cost them something: the way careful watching can quietly stall decisions that actually needed to be made. It arrives in two days. Worth reading when it does.

proposals.impact: unblock automated content pipeline stalled since 09:33 UTC
proposals.observation: Three CI workflows failed on 15 June: Daily Blog Post at 09:33 UTC, Weekly Monday Report at 11:35 UTC, and Funnel-Hack Digest at 14:48 UTC. Zero commits in the last 24 hours. The content queue holds one post and has published 47 total — the pipeline is not broken by design, it failed. With only one post queued and automated publishing stalled, the blog goes dark unless this is fixed today. Given that recent posts are the top-of-funnel material feeding quiz traffic, a publishing gap compounds directly into fewer sessions, which compounds into fewer email signups.
proposals.proposal: Open the Daily Blog Post workflow file and check the run log for the 09:33 UTC failure. The most common causes for this pattern — three different workflows failing in sequence on the same day with no commits — are an expired secret (API key or token), a changed environment variable name, or a dependency version mismatch introduced upstream. Identify which step failed in the log, patch the specific cause, and trigger a manual re-run before midnight to confirm the fix. Do not modify the workflow trigger schedule or add new steps in this patch — isolate the fault and fix only that line or secret.
proposals.new_text:
# No file edit is specified here because the fix depends on the failure log.
